comments.content: This course was really helpful and easy to follow.
The explanations are clear and the exercises are useful.
Great JavaScript course. I learned a lot.
The React examples are very practical.
Very good explanation of Next.js App Router.
The design exercises were really useful.

questions.content: How long does it take for SEO changes to show in Google results?
Do I need paid tools to follow the exercises?
What is the difference between let and const?
When should I use useEffect instead of an event handler?
Is the App Router required, or can I still use the Pages Router?

quizQuestions.question: What is the main goal of SEO?

options.text: Increase organic (unpaid) traffic by improving visibility in search results
Buy ads to appear at the top of search results
Increase the number of social media followers
Make a website load without an internet connection

quizQuestions.explanation: SEO focuses on earning higher rankings in unpaid search results so more people find your site organically.

quizQuestions.question: Which HTML tag defines the clickable headline shown for a page in search results?
quizQuestions.explanation: Search engines usually use the title tag as the title link in results, so it should describe the page clearly.

quizQuestions.question: Which of these is an example of off-page SEO?

options.text: Compressing the images on your pages
Earning backlinks from other reputable websites
Adding headings to structure your content

quizQuestions.explanation: Off-page SEO covers signals outside your site, such as backlinks. The other options are on-page optimizations.

quizQuestions.question: Which statement about JavaScript is true?

options.text: It can only run inside Java applications
It must be compiled to machine code before every run
It is only used to style web pages
It runs in web browsers and, with Node.js, on servers too

quizQuestions.explanation: JavaScript runs in every modern browser and, through runtimes like Node.js, outside the browser as well.

quizQuestions.question: What will this code return?
quizQuestions.explanation: In JavaScript, arrays are objects, so typeof [] returns 'object'.

quizQuestions.question: What will this code print?
quizQuestions.explanation: The arrow function returns n * 2, so double(4) returns 8.

quizQuestions.question: What does this code print?
quizQuestions.explanation: map() returns a new array with the callback applied to every item.

quizQuestions.question: What must the name of a React component start with?
quizQuestions.explanation: React treats lowercase tags as HTML elements, so a component like Button must start with a capital letter.

quizQuestions.question: What does useState return?

options.text: An array with the current state value and a function to update it
An object with get and set methods
A promise that resolves to the state

quizQuestions.explanation: useState returns a two-item array: the state value and its setter, which is why array destructuring is used.

quizQuestions.question: When does this effect run?

options.text: Once, after the component's first render
Before the component renders for the first time

quizQuestions.explanation: An empty dependency array means the effect has nothing to react to, so it runs once after mount.

quizQuestions.question: What naming rule must a custom hook follow?

options.text: Its name must start with a capital letter
It must be defined inside a class component
Its name must start with use

quizQuestions.explanation: Names starting with use let React and the linter recognize hooks and enforce the Rules of Hooks.

quizQuestions.question: In the Next.js App Router, which file defines the UI for a route?
quizQuestions.explanation: A route becomes publicly accessible when it contains a page file, such as app/about/page.tsx.

quizQuestions.question: Which file wraps shared UI around child pages and stays mounted when navigating between them?
quizQuestions.explanation: layout.tsx preserves state and does not re-render when navigating between sibling routes.

quizQuestions.question: What does this directive do?

options.text: Forces the page to be rendered only at build time
Marks the file as a Client Component so it can use state and browser APIs
Disables TypeScript checking in the file
Turns the component into an API route

quizQuestions.explanation: In the App Router, components are Server Components by default. "use client" opts in to client-side interactivity such as useState.

quizQuestions.question: Why can this component use await directly?

options.text: Because await works in any React component
Because fetch blocks the browser on purpose
Because it is a Server Component, and Server Components can be async
Because Next.js converts it into a class component

quizQuestions.explanation: Server Components can be async functions, so you can fetch data on the server without useEffect.

quizQuestions.question: What does visual hierarchy do in a design?

options.text: Makes every element the same size
Guides users' attention to the most important elements first

quizQuestions.explanation: Size, color, contrast and spacing signal what matters most, so users scan the screen in the right order.

quizQuestions.question: Where are complementary colors located on the color wheel?

options.text: Three colors apart, forming a triangle
At the same position with different brightness

quizQuestions.explanation: Complementary pairs such as blue and orange sit opposite each other and create strong contrast.

quizQuestions.question: What is a wireframe?

options.text: A low-fidelity layout that shows structure without final visuals
A coded prototype with real data
A style guide of brand colors

quizQuestions.explanation: Wireframes focus on layout and content placement before colors, images and typography are decided.

quizQuestions.question: What is the main aim of content marketing?

options.text: Lower the price of every product
Attract and retain an audience with valuable, relevant content
Send as many messages as possible each day

quizQuestions.explanation: Content marketing builds trust and attracts customers by being useful, not by interrupting them.

quizQuestions.question: Which email metric shows the percentage of recipients who clicked a link?
quizQuestions.explanation: CTR measures clicks relative to delivered emails. Open rate measures opens, not clicks.

quizQuestions.question: In Google Analytics, what is a session?

options.text: A group of a user's interactions with your site within a given time frame

quizQuestions.explanation: A session bundles interactions such as page views and events that happen during one visit.

quizQuestions.question: What does this code print?
quizQuestions.explanation: Numbers with a decimal point are floats in Python.

quizQuestions.question: What does this loop print?
quizQuestions.explanation: range(3) generates 0, 1, 2. The stop value is excluded.

quizQuestions.question: What does this code print?
quizQuestions.explanation: Negative indexes count from the end, so -1 is the last item.

quizQuestions.question: What happens with this code?
quizQuestions.code:
let id: string | number;
id = true;

options.text: TypeScript reports an error because boolean is not assignable to string | number
It works and id becomes true
It converts true to the number 1
It throws an error only at runtime

quizQuestions.explanation: A union type accepts only its listed members, and the check happens at compile time.

quizQuestions.question: What does T represent in this function?

options.text: A type parameter that is set when the function is called

quizQuestions.explanation: Generics let a function work with many types while keeping the relationship between input and output types.

quizQuestions.question: What does Partial<User> do?

options.text: Makes all properties of User optional

quizQuestions.explanation: Partial<T> builds a type where every property of T is optional, which is useful for update payloads.

quizQuestions.question: Which semantic HTML element is meant for the main navigation links of a page?
quizQuestions.explanation: <nav> tells browsers and assistive technology that the block contains navigation links. <div> has no meaning.

quizQuestions.question: In the CSS box model, which order lists the layers from the inside out?
quizQuestions.explanation: Content sits in the middle, surrounded by padding, then the border, then the outer margin.

quizQuestions.question: What does this CSS create?

options.text: One column that is three times wider
A flex row with three items

quizQuestions.explanation: repeat(3, 1fr) defines three columns that share the available width equally.

quizQuestions.question: What will this route send for a request to /users/42?
quizQuestions.explanation: The :id segment is a route parameter available on req.params, so req.params.id is the string "42".

quizQuestions.question: What must a middleware function call to pass control to the next handler?
quizQuestions.explanation: Unless it ends the response, middleware must call next(), otherwise the request hangs.

quizQuestions.question: Which HTTP method is conventionally used to create a new resource in a REST API?
quizQuestions.explanation: POST creates a resource, GET reads, PUT/PATCH update and DELETE removes.

quizQuestions.question: What does this query return?
quizQuestions.code: SELECT name FROM students WHERE age > 18;

options.text: The names of students older than 18
The number of students older than 18

quizQuestions.explanation: SELECT picks the name column and WHERE keeps only rows where age is greater than 18.

quizQuestions.question: What does an INNER JOIN return?

options.text: All rows from the left table, matched or not
Only rows with matching values in both tables
Every combination of rows from both tables

quizQuestions.explanation: The second option describes a LEFT JOIN and the last one a CROSS JOIN.

quizQuestions.question: Which clause filters groups after a GROUP BY?
quizQuestions.explanation: WHERE filters rows before grouping. HAVING filters the aggregated groups.

quizQuestions.question: What is the main purpose of database normalization?

options.text: Reduce data redundancy and improve data integrity
Store all data in a single large table
Remove the need for primary keys

quizQuestions.explanation: Normalization splits data into related tables so each fact is stored once.

quizQuestions.question: Which command creates a new branch and switches to it?
quizQuestions.explanation: git checkout -b creates and switches in one step. git switch -c feature does the same in newer Git versions.

quizQuestions.question: What does this command do?

options.text: Creates a new branch called origin
Uploads your local main commits to the remote named origin

quizQuestions.explanation: git push sends your local commits to the given remote and branch.

quizQuestions.question: In a conflicted file, what does the part between <<<<<<< HEAD and ======= represent?
quizQuestions.code:
<<<<<<< HEAD
const title = "Home";
=======
const title = "Welcome";
>>>>>>> feature

options.text: Your current branch's version of the conflicting lines

quizQuestions.explanation: Above ======= is HEAD (your current branch). Below it is the incoming change from the other branch.

quizQuestions.question: What is a key difference between containers and virtual machines?

options.text: Containers share the host OS kernel, while VMs run a full guest OS
Containers always run a full guest operating system
Only one container can run per host

quizQuestions.explanation: Sharing the kernel makes containers lighter and faster to start than VMs.

quizQuestions.question: What does -p 8080:80 do in this command?

options.text: Maps port 80 on the host to port 8080 in the container
Maps port 8080 on the host to port 80 in the container
Limits the container to 8080 MB of memory

quizQuestions.explanation: The format is host_port:container_port.

quizQuestions.question: Why use a Docker volume?

options.text: To persist data beyond the lifetime of a container
To give the container more CPU

quizQuestions.explanation: Data inside a container's writable layer is lost when it is removed. Volumes keep it.

quizQuestions.question: What is Docker Compose mainly used for?

options.text: Building a single image without a Dockerfile
Defining and running multi-container applications from a YAML file

quizQuestions.explanation: A compose file describes services, networks and volumes so an app starts with one command.

quizQuestions.question: What does the p-4 class do?

options.text: Adds padding of 1rem (16px) on all sides
Sets the font size to 4 points

quizQuestions.explanation: In default Tailwind, one spacing step is 0.25rem, so 4 equals 1rem.

quizQuestions.question: When does md:flex apply display: flex?

options.text: At the medium breakpoint (768px) and wider

quizQuestions.explanation: Tailwind is mobile-first: unprefixed utilities apply everywhere, prefixed ones from that breakpoint up.

quizQuestions.question: Which prefix makes a utility apply only in dark mode?
quizQuestions.explanation: Example: dark:bg-gray-900 applies the background only when dark mode is active.

quizQuestions.question: What does this code print?
quizQuestions.code:
import numpy as np

arr = np.array([1, 2, 3])
print(arr * 2)
quizQuestions.explanation: NumPy applies operations element-wise. A plain Python list [1, 2, 3] * 2 would repeat the list instead.

quizQuestions.question: What does df.head() return by default?

options.text: The first 5 rows of the DataFrame

quizQuestions.explanation: head() shows the first 5 rows. tail() shows the last ones and describe() gives statistics.

quizQuestions.question: What does this code do?

options.text: Removes rows that contain missing values

quizQuestions.explanation: dropna() removes rows with NaN values. fillna() fills them and drop_duplicates() removes duplicates.

quizQuestions.question: Which kind of problem is linear regression designed for?

options.text: Assigning an email to spam or not spam
Predicting a continuous numeric value, such as a house price

quizQuestions.explanation: Regression predicts numbers. Classification predicts categories.

quizQuestions.question: Which of these is a classification task?

options.text: Predicting whether a customer will churn (yes or no)

quizQuestions.explanation: Classification predicts discrete categories. The others predict continuous numbers.

quizQuestions.question: Why do we split data into training and test sets?

options.text: To evaluate the model on data it has not seen during training
To increase the amount of data

quizQuestions.explanation: Testing on unseen data gives an honest estimate of how the model performs in the real world.

quizQuestions.question: What is overfitting?

options.text: A model that is too simple to capture patterns
A model fits the training data very well but performs poorly on new data
A model that trains too quickly
A model trained on too many examples

quizQuestions.explanation: Overfitting means memorizing noise in the training data. The second option describes underfitting.

quizQuestions.question: Which Dart keyword declares a variable that can be assigned only once?
quizQuestions.explanation: final variables are set once at runtime. const creates compile-time constants, and var can be reassigned.

quizQuestions.question: Which widget type should you use when part of the UI must change after user interaction?
quizQuestions.explanation: StatefulWidget holds mutable state and rebuilds when setState is called. StatelessWidget never changes by itself.

quizQuestions.question: What does this code do?

options.text: Pushes DetailsPage onto the navigation stack so it appears on top
Clears the whole history and shows DetailsPage
Removes the current screen from memory
Opens DetailsPage in a new app window

quizQuestions.explanation: push adds a route to the stack, and Navigator.pop returns to the previous screen.

quizQuestions.question: What do the letters in the CIA triad stand for?
quizQuestions.explanation: The CIA triad is the core model of information security.

quizQuestions.question: What is phishing?

options.text: Guessing passwords with every possible combination
Tricking people into revealing sensitive information through fake messages or sites

quizQuestions.explanation: The other options describe a DDoS attack, brute force and ransomware.

quizQuestions.question: Which statement about asymmetric encryption is true?

options.text: It uses the same key to encrypt and decrypt
It is only used for hashing passwords
It uses a public key and a private key pair

quizQuestions.explanation: Data encrypted with a public key can only be decrypted with the matching private key.

quizQuestions.question: What does the inverted pyramid structure recommend?

options.text: Put the most important information first, then supporting details
Start with background and save the key point for the end
Use the longest paragraphs at the top
Place the call to action only in the title

quizQuestions.explanation: Readers get the key message immediately, even if they stop reading early.

quizQuestions.question: What does the AIDA copywriting model stand for?
quizQuestions.explanation: AIDA guides readers from noticing the message to taking action.

quizQuestions.question: Where should you naturally include your primary keyword when writing for SEO?

options.text: Repeated as many times as possible in every sentence
In the title, early in the introduction and in relevant headings

quizQuestions.explanation: Natural placement in prominent spots helps. Keyword stuffing hurts readers and rankings.

quizQuestions.question: What does Auto Layout do in Figma?

options.text: Makes a frame automatically resize and space its children as content changes

quizQuestions.explanation: Auto Layout works like flexbox: spacing, padding and direction adapt as content is added or removed.

quizQuestions.question: What happens to instances when you edit their main component?

options.text: The changes propagate to all instances

quizQuestions.explanation: Instances stay linked to the main component, except for properties you have overridden.

quizQuestions.question: What do you create to make a prototype interactive in Figma?

options.text: A new page for each frame
Connections between frames with an interaction such as On click

quizQuestions.explanation: In Prototype mode you link frames and choose a trigger and an action, for example On click, Navigate to.
